============================================================
1. OBJECTIVE
============================================================

S3.20 established that individual constraints behave differently
under free relational amalgamation and under pullback to the
P2.3 carrier.

S3.21 formulates a precise criterion for a delimited logical
fragment. The target is not a classification of all first-order
theories. It is a two-stage preservation result:

  Stage A:
  Determine when a free relational amalgam preserves a
  universal Horn theory.

  Stage B:
  Determine when inverse-image pullback along the quotient map
  preserves that theory.

The central distinction is between:
  (i) guarded, side-local Horn triggers;
  (ii) mixed triggers whose variables can occupy both exclusive
       sides of the amalgam;
  (iii) equality-generating conclusions, which can fail under
        non-injective pullback.

No claim is made that all universal Horn theories are preserved.


============================================================
2. FORMAL SETUP
============================================================

Let Sigma be a finite or arbitrary function-free relational
signature. Relation symbols have fixed finite arities. Equality
is interpreted as actual identity.

Let C be a common induced substructure of A and B. Replace the
embeddings by isomorphic copies so that:

  A intersect B = C.

Let D be the free relational amalgam with universe:

  |D| = |A| union |B|.

For every n-ary relation symbol R in Sigma, define:

  R_D = R_A union R_B.

Thus a tuple belongs to R_D exactly when it belongs to at least
one side relation. No new mixed tuple is added.

The embeddings A -> D and B -> D are induced embeddings.

A universal Horn clause has the form:

  forall x1,...,xn:
    (alpha1 AND ... AND alphak) IMPLIES beta

where each alpha_i is either:
  - a relational atom R(t1,...,tm); or
  - a positive equality t=u.

The head beta is one of:
  - a relational atom;
  - an equality;
  - falsity, written BOTTOM.

Terms are variables only, because the signature is function-free.

The body contains no disequality and no negated relational atom.
This restriction is essential for the pullback result below.

A universal Horn theory T is a set of such clauses.


============================================================
3. SIDE-LOCALITY LEMMA
============================================================

For an assignment s of the variables of a clause into D, call
the assignment SIDE-LOCAL if its entire range is contained in A
or its entire range is contained in B.

Call it MIXED if its range meets both:

  A minus C
  B minus C.

LEMMA 3.1:
If A and B satisfy a universal Horn clause and an assignment s
is side-local, then the clause is satisfied in D under s.

PROOF:

Assume the range of s is contained in A.

Every relational body atom true in D under s is true in A,
because the relation on A is the induced restriction of the
relation in D. Every positive equality true in D is also true
in A.

Therefore, if the body is true in D under s, it is true in A.
Since A satisfies the clause, its head is true in A, or the
body cannot be true when the head is BOTTOM.

If the head is relational, its tuple remains present in D.
If the head is equality, equality remains true in D.
The BOTTOM case cannot occur with a true body.

The proof for an assignment whose range is contained in B is
identical.

Therefore every possible violation of the clause in D must
come from a mixed assignment.

QED.


============================================================
4. EXACT MIXED-TRIGGER CRITERION
============================================================

THEOREM 4.1:
Let T be a universal Horn theory in the fragment defined in
Section 2. Let D be the free relational amalgam of A and B over
C, and assume A and B satisfy T.

Then:

  D satisfies T

IFF

for every clause in T and every mixed assignment s into D,
if the complete body is true under s, then the head is true
under s.

For a BOTTOM head, this means that no mixed assignment may make
the body true.

PROOF:

Necessity is immediate from D satisfying T.

For sufficiency, take any clause and any assignment s into D.
If s is side-local, Lemma 3.1 gives satisfaction.
If s is mixed, the stated criterion gives satisfaction.
These two cases exhaust all assignments.

Thus every clause in T is satisfied in D.

QED.

INTERPRETATION:

The criterion isolates the exact failure mode of free
amalgamation. The input structures already satisfy T. A failure
can arise only when a clause receives a mixed assignment whose
body becomes true across the two sides while its head is absent.

This is an exact semantic test for a specified span and its
free amalgam. It is not, by itself, a purely syntactic
classification of all theories with the amalgamation property.


============================================================
5. GUARDED UNIVERSAL HORN FRAGMENT
============================================================

DEFINITION 5.1:
A universal Horn clause is RELATIONALLY GUARDED if its body
contains a relational atom G(t1,...,tm) such that every variable
occurring anywhere in the clause occurs among
t1,...,tm.

The atom G is called a guard for the clause.

Repeated variables in the guard are allowed. The guard may be
any relation symbol of the signature.

THEOREM 5.2:
The free relational amalgam of two models of a relationally
guarded universal Horn theory is again a model of that theory.

PROOF:

Take one guarded clause and an arbitrary assignment s into D.

If its body is false, the implication is satisfied.

Suppose its body is true. In particular, its guard atom is true
in D under s.

By definition of the free relation union, the guard tuple
belongs to G_A or G_B. Since the guard contains every variable
of the clause, the complete range of s lies in that same side.

Thus s is side-local.

By Lemma 3.1, the clause is satisfied in D under s.

Since the clause and assignment were arbitrary, D satisfies
the whole guarded theory.

QED.

COROLLARY 5.3:
Every class axiomatized by a relationally guarded universal Horn
theory has the free relational amalgamation property for
induced embeddings, provided the common structure is an
induced common substructure and the signature is function-free.

The amalgam is strong because the underlying pushout identifies
only the common substructure.

SCOPE:

This corollary concerns the free relational amalgam in the
specified function-free relational setting. It does not cover
arbitrary universal Horn theories, function symbols, arbitrary
negated atoms, or additional realization and dynamical data.


============================================================
6. WHY THE S3.20 COUNTEREXAMPLES FALL OUTSIDE THE GUARDED
FRAGMENT
============================================================

6.1 SYMMETRY

Clause:

  forall x,y:
    R(x,y) IMPLIES R(y,x).

The body atom R(x,y) contains every variable of the clause.
It is a guard.

Therefore free union preserves symmetry.

6.2 IRREFLEXIVITY

Clause:

  forall x:
    R(x,x) IMPLIES BOTTOM.

The body atom contains every variable.
It is a guard.

Therefore free union preserves irreflexivity.

6.3 TRANSITIVITY

Clause:

  forall x,y,z:
    (R(x,y) AND R(y,z)) IMPLIES R(x,z).

Neither body atom contains all three variables.
The two premises can be supported by different sides.

The S3.20 span:

  C = {c}
  A = {a,c}, R_A = {(a,c)}
  B = {c,b}, R_B = {(c,b)}

activates the body with x=a, y=c, z=b, but the free union
does not contain R(a,b).

Thus the clause is not preserved by free union in general.

This does not rule out a non-free strong amalgam. S3.20 gave
one by adding the required edge a R b.

6.4 FUNCTIONALITY

Clause:

  forall x,y,z:
    (R(x,y) AND R(x,z)) IMPLIES y=z.

No single body atom contains all three variables.
The two premises can be supported on opposite sides.

In the S3.20 span, the free union contains R(c,a) and R(c,b)
with a distinct from b. The equality head fails.

This is a mixed-trigger failure. The same span has no strong
amalgam in the class of functional relations.

6.5 ACYCLICITY

Acyclicity can be expressed by the infinite family of denial
clauses forbidding directed cycles of each finite length.

For a cycle of length at least three, its edge premises can be
distributed across the two sides. There is no single edge atom
covering all cycle variables.

The S3.20 cycle-forcing span therefore lies outside the
guarded fragment and has no acyclic amalgam at all.

CONCLUSION:

The guarded condition is a meaningful sufficient syntactic
criterion. The S3.20 counterexamples do not refute it. They
instead show why the broader claim that all universal Horn
constraints are preserved would be false.


============================================================
7. PULLBACK PRESERVATION THEOREM
============================================================

Let pi:X -> Q be a surjective map. For each n-ary relation R_Q
on Q, define its inverse-image relation on X by:

  R_X(x1,...,xn) IFF R_Q(pi(x1),...,pi(xn)).

This is the relational pullback used in the P2.3 quotient
construction.

THEOREM 7.1:
Let T be a universal Horn theory in the fragment of Section 2.
Assume every clause has either:
  (a) a relational atom as its head; or
  (b) BOTTOM as its head.

Then:

  Q satisfies T
  IMPLIES
  X satisfies T

under the inverse-image interpretation of every relation.

PROOF:

Take a clause and an assignment s of its variables into X.
Suppose the body is true in X.

For every relational body atom, the definition of inverse image
implies that the corresponding atom is true in Q under pi composed
with s.

For every positive equality in the body, equality of elements
in X implies equality of their images in Q.

Therefore the entire body is true in Q under the projected
assignment.

Since Q satisfies the clause, either:
  (i) the head is BOTTOM, which is impossible with a true body;
  (ii) the relational head is true in Q.

In case (ii), the definition of inverse-image relation makes
the head true in X under s.

Thus the clause is satisfied in X. This holds for every clause
and assignment.

QED.

IMPORTANT LIMIT:

The theorem does not include equality as a possible head.
A quotient equality pi(x)=pi(y) does not imply x=y.


============================================================
8. EQUALITY-GENERATING HEADS AND FIBER OBSTRUCTIONS
============================================================

A universal Horn clause with an equality head is an
equality-generating dependency.

Example: functionality

  forall x,y,z:
    (R(x,y) AND R(x,z)) IMPLIES y=z.

Even if Q satisfies this clause, its pullback X need not.

COUNTEREXAMPLE:

Let:

  Q = {q,r}
  R_Q = {(q,r)}

Then R_Q is functional.

Let:

  X = {x,y1,y2}
  pi(x)=q
  pi(y1)=r
  pi(y2)=r
  y1 != y2.

The pullback contains:

  R_X(x,y1)
  R_X(x,y2).

Functionality would require y1=y2, which is false.

Therefore inverse-image pullback does not preserve functionality
in general.

CLAUSE-SPECIFIC FIBER CONDITION:

For a clause whose head is the equality u=v, a sufficient
condition for pullback preservation is:

For every assignment in X that satisfies the clause body,
the equality of the projected head values forced by Q must
already be equality of the original values in X.

For a functionality clause, this means that every target fiber
over an R_Q-successor of a source point has size at most one.

Global injectivity of pi is a stronger sufficient condition,
but it is not generally available in a nontrivial quotient.

Thus equality-generating constraints require a separate
fiber audit. They cannot be treated as ordinary relational
heads.


============================================================
9. COMBINED QUOTIENT-AMALGAMATION AND PULLBACK COROLLARY
============================================================

COROLLARY 9.1:

Let A and B be models of a function-free relational theory T,
with common induced substructure C. Form their free relational
amalgam D.

Assume:
  1. T is relationally guarded universal Horn;
  2. every clause head is either a relational atom or BOTTOM;
  3. there are no function symbols, disequality premises, or
     negated relational premises.

Then:
  (a) D satisfies T;
  (b) for every surjective quotient map pi:X -> D, the
      inverse-image relational structure on X also satisfies T;
  (c) the resulting amalgam on X remains strong whenever the
      underlying carrier construction is the P2.3 strong
      amalgam and the embeddings are the P2.3 embeddings.

PROOF:

Part (a) is Theorem 5.2.
Part (b) is Theorem 7.1.
Part (c) follows from the underlying P2.3 carrier construction;
the relational interpretation adds no new identifications.

QED.

EXTENSION WITH EQUALITY HEADS:

If T includes equality-generating heads, part (a) remains valid
for guarded clauses, because their assignments are side-local.
Part (b) then requires the clause-specific fiber condition of
Section 8. Global injectivity of pi is sufficient but often
too strong.

This is the two-stage criterion relevant to the P2.3 pipeline:

  INPUT MODELS
      |
      v
  FREE QUOTIENT RELATIONAL AMALGAM
      |
      | guarded Horn preservation
      v
  QUOTIENT MODEL OF T
      |
      | inverse-image pullback
      v
  P2.3 CARRIER MODEL OF T

The two arrows have distinct proof obligations.


============================================================
10. LOOP AUDIT AND NON-IMPLICATIONS
============================================================

LOOP AUDIT:

TARGET:
Prove preservation for the explicitly defined guarded Horn
fragment and the stated pullback fragment.

INDEPENDENT PREMISES:
- The free relation is the union of side relations.
- Each input structure satisfies the Horn clauses.
- A guard atom contains every variable of its clause.
- Pullback relations are defined by inverse image.
- Positive equality is preserved by applying a map.

CONCLUSION-SMUGGLING CHECK:
The conclusion is not built into the definition of a guard.
The proof uses the guard to show that any assignment activating
the body must lie entirely in one side. This is independently
derived from the free-union semantics.

PULLBACK CHECK:
The proof uses only the inverse-image definition and the
satisfaction of the quotient structure. It does not assume that
the original carrier already satisfies the target constraint.

NON-IMPLICATIONS:

1. Not every universal Horn theory is guarded.
2. Not every universal Horn theory is preserved by free
   relational amalgamation.
3. Free-union failure does not imply failure of all strong
   amalgams.
4. Failure of strong amalgamation does not imply failure of
   every non-strong amalgam.
5. Quotient-level satisfaction does not imply pullback
   satisfaction for equality-generating heads.
6. The result does not cover operations, dynamics, Markov
   kernels, realization maps, response maps, or the complete
   OMEGA-ISOP architecture.
7. No physical interpretation or physical law follows from
   this relational theorem.


============================================================
11. RESULT MATRIX
============================================================

Constraint fragment:
Relationally guarded universal Horn

Free quotient union:
Preserved

Pullback with relational head or BOTTOM:
Preserved

Pullback with equality head:
Requires a fiber condition


Constraint:
Transitivity

Guarded:
No, in the standard binary formulation

Free quotient union:
Can fail

Alternative strong amalgam:
Exists in the S3.20 example


Constraint:
Functionality

Guarded:
No

Free quotient union:
Can fail

Alternative strong amalgam:
Impossible in the S3.20 example

Pullback:
Can fail even when the quotient relation is functional


Constraint:
Acyclicity

Guarded:
Not covered by the finite-cycle denial clauses

Free quotient union:
Can fail

Alternative amalgam:
Impossible in the S3.20 cycle-forcing example


============================================================
12. APPLICATION TO OMEGA-ISOP
============================================================

P2.3 supplies:
  - the quotient sets Q_A, Q_B, Q_C;
  - their set pushout Q;
  - the strong carrier pushout S_P;
  - the quotient projection pi_P:S_P -> Q;
  - apartness defined by inequality of quotient images.

S3.19 supplies the quotient-level relational construction for
coordinatewise quotient-invariant relations.

S3.20 shows that additional constraints must be checked under
both quotient amalgamation and pullback.

S3.21 adds a sufficient logical fragment:

If the quotient-level constraints are relationally guarded
universal Horn clauses with relational heads or BOTTOM, then
the free quotient relational amalgam satisfies them, and their
pullbacks to S_P satisfy them.

If equality-generating heads are included, an additional
fiber condition is required.

This does not establish that the actual realization, dynamics,
Markov, response, or persistence structures of Volume II satisfy
the guard or pullback hypotheses. Those structures require
separate typed definitions and compatibility proofs.

No change to the definitions of P2.3, P2.4, or the Frozen Core
is proposed or enacted.


============================================================
13. FINAL STATUS
============================================================

S3.21 RESULT:

PROVED:
1. Exact mixed-trigger criterion for a specified free
   relational amalgam and universal Horn theory.
2. Free-amalgam preservation for relationally guarded
   universal Horn theories.
3. Pullback preservation for universal Horn clauses with
   relational heads or BOTTOM, under positive-equality bodies.
4. Equality-head obstruction and a clause-specific fiber
   condition.
5. Combined two-stage preservation corollary for the stated
   guarded fragment.

NOT PROVED:
1. Preservation of arbitrary universal Horn theories.
2. A necessary-and-sufficient syntactic classification of all
   theories with free amalgamation.
3. General amalgamation for transitive, functional, or acyclic
   relation classes.
4. Preservation of all OMEGA-ISOP operations and dynamics.
5. A complete Stage 3 compatibility theorem.

EVIDENCE CLASS:
MATHEMATICALLY PROVED UNDER THE EXPLICIT FUNCTION-FREE
RELATIONAL ASSUMPTIONS; NOT CANONICALLY ACCEPTED.

CANONICAL STATUS:
NOT ACCEPTED.

RL REGISTRATION:
NONE.

UNCHANGED.
